compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

An `s3://` ticket-store remote is only safe with a `git-remote-s3` helper that has the
`IfNoneMatch` per-ref lock: a live experiment this session proved that a client **without**
that lock is exactly what leaves two `<sha>.bundle` files for one ref, producing the
multiple-bundles corruption that makes the store unclonable. Today nothing stops rebar from
driving an `s3://` remote with a missing or too-old helper — the failure would surface later
as silent store corruption rather than at the point of misconfiguration.

The sibling story ("Declare the optional [s3] extra…", now landed) provides
`require_s3_helper()` in `src/rebar/_optional.py`, which confirms the helper is on `PATH` and
`>=0.3.2`, raising `OptionalDependencyError` (message naming `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`
and the `>=0.3.2` minimum) otherwise. This story **wires that guard in** so any store
operation that would drive an `s3://` remote fails closed early with that actionable message.

## Approach

Detect "S3 mode" by the **remote URL scheme** — no new config key (reuse the existing
`sync.remote`, `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` `SyncConfig.remote`). Treat a remote as S3 mode
iff its resolved URL starts with `s3://` or `s3+zip://` (git-remote-s3's own schemes).

Add one small internal preflight helper in `src/rebar/_store/push.py`,
`_require_s3_helper_if_s3_url(remote_url: str) -> None`, that takes an already-resolved remote
URL string and, when it starts with `s3://`/`s3+zip://`, calls
`rebar._optional.require_s3_helper()` and lets its `OptionalDependencyError` propagate; for any
other scheme (or an empty string) it is a no-op. Taking the URL as an argument keeps it pure
and lets each call site reuse the resolution it *already* performs — no new gitutil shell-out
is added (the review flagged `resolve_remote_url` as redundant with the existing seams below).

**The best-effort contract, resolved explicitly.** `push_tickets_branch` is best-effort by
default (returns `None` on delivery failure; raises `PushDeliveryError` only when
`strict=True`), and it has **two** auto-push callers: `write_and_push`
(`src/rebar/_store/event_append.py`, the append-event family) calls it **without** a
try/except, and `push_after_commit` (`src/rebar/_store/push.py`, the inline-commit paths —
`transition`/`reopen`/`claim`/`compact`/`delete`) wraps it in a best-effort
`except Exception` that must be made to **re-raise** `OptionalDependencyError` so it does
not swallow the deliberate S3 fail-closed override. A missing/too-old S3
helper is **not** a transient delivery hiccup to swallow — it is a hard misconfiguration that
must halt loudly to prevent the unlocked push that corrupts the store. So the S3 preflight
raises `OptionalDependencyError` **unconditionally, independent of `strict`**, deliberately
overriding best-effort. Because `write_and_push` does not catch it, the raise propagates and
aborts the write with the actionable message and a non-zero exit; the local commit
`stage_and_commit` already made is durable, and only the corrupting push is prevented (the
store stays locally consistent and `fsck` surfaces `PUSH_PENDING`). This deliberate exception
to the best-effort contract is the intended fail-closed behavior the AC requires.

Call sites, all keyed off the **already-resolved** URL (no second resolution):

- **`push.py` synchronous (`always`) path** — `push_tickets_branch` already resolves the
  configured remote's URL at `src/rebar/_store/push.py:418`
  (`remote_url = _git(base_path, "remote", "get-url", remote)`). Immediately after that
  resolution succeeds (i.e. after the existing `returncode != 0` / `remote-not-found` skip at
  lines ~419-426, so an **unresolvable/unset remote keeps its existing best-effort skip and is
  NOT treated as S3**), call `_require_s3_helper_if_s3_url(remote_url.stdout.strip())` before
  the push retry loop.
- **`push.py` `async` arm** — before it detaches the synchronous child (lines ~361-401),
  resolve the configured remote URL the same way and call the preflight, so an async-mode
  misconfiguration also fails fast **in the parent** (surfacing the message) rather than only
  inside the detached child whose stderr is discarded. The `off` arm is left untouched (it
  never pushes, so there is no corruption risk and no helper requirement).
- **`src/rebar/_commands/init.py` init/mount** — in `_mount_or_create_branch` (line ~383),
  after `remote_name = tickets_remote(repo)` is resolved, resolve its URL with the module's
  existing `_git(repo, "remote", "get-url", remote_name)` and call the same preflight, so a
  misconfigured `s3://` remote is caught at setup, not at first write.

Rationale: keying off the URL scheme reuses the field git-remote-s3 already keys off, needs
zero schema/migration work, and keeps the blast radius to `s3://`/`s3+zip://` remotes only;
guarding at init (fail-fast at config time) plus both push arms (belt-and-suspenders on the
hot write path) funnels every path through the single tested `require_s3_helper()` seam.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_store/push.py` — add `_require_s3_helper_if_s3_url()`; call it in the synchronous
  `always` path (after the existing URL resolution at line ~418) and in the `async` arm before
  detaching. No new remote-URL resolution is introduced (the line-418 `_git ... remote get-url`
  is reused).
- `src/rebar/_commands/init.py` — call the preflight in `_mount_or_create_branch` after the
  remote name is resolved, using the module's existing `_git` shell-out.
- `tests/` — CLI/subprocess tests for the fail-closed and no-op behavior.

Explicitly **not** in scope: no new helper in `src/rebar/_store/gitutil.py` (the existing
`_git ... remote get-url` at `push.py:418` and init.py's `_git` are reused); no config schema
change.

## Testing

Tier: **CLI subprocess** against a real temporary git repo configured with an `s3://`
`sync.remote` (no AWS calls needed — the guard fails before any network I/O). Oracles:
- Failure (helper missing, init): with `git-remote-s3` not on `PATH` and `sync.remote` an
  `s3://` URL, `rebar init` exits non-zero and prints the message naming
  `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`.
- Failure (helper missing, push): the same configuration on a synchronous write/push path
  exits non-zero with the same actionable message.
- Edge (helper too old): monkeypatch the version probe to `0.2.9` → same fail-closed message
  naming the `>=0.3.2` minimum, on both init and push.
- Edge (`s3+zip://` scheme): with an `s3+zip://` `sync.remote` and the helper absent, init/push
  fail closed identically (the scheme is treated as S3 mode).
- Happy / no-regression (non-S3 remote): with a `file://` or GitHub-style remote, the preflight
  is a no-op and init/push succeed with **no** helper installed and no behavior change.
- No-regression (unresolvable remote): with `sync.remote` naming a remote that does not exist
  (`git remote get-url` fails), the push path keeps its existing best-effort `remote-not-found`
  skip and does **not** raise the S3 error (the missing URL is not misread as S3 mode).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] With `sync.remote` pointing at an `s3://` URL and the helper absent, store init and the
      synchronous push path both **exit non-zero** with a single actionable message naming
      `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`. The preflight raises `OptionalDependencyError`
      **unconditionally** (independent of `push_tickets_branch`'s best-effort `strict` flag),
      propagating through the uncaught `write_and_push` call and the `OptionalDependencyError` re-raise in `push_after_commit`. Verified by the init and push
      CLI-subprocess failure oracles.
- [x] With the helper present but below `0.3.2`, the same paths fail closed naming the
      `>=0.3.2` minimum. Verified by the too-old edge oracle.
- [x] An `s3+zip://` `sync.remote` is treated as S3 mode and fails closed identically when the
      helper is absent. Verified by the `s3+zip://` edge oracle.
- [x] With a non-`s3://`/`s3+zip://` `sync.remote`, the preflight is a no-op: init and push
      succeed with no helper installed and no behavior change; and a remote whose URL cannot be
      resolved keeps the existing best-effort `remote-not-found` skip (it is not misread as S3).
      Verified by the no-regression and unresolvable-remote oracles.
- [x] S3 mode is detected purely from the remote URL scheme (no new config key added) and no
      new remote-URL resolution seam is introduced — the existing `_git ... remote get-url` at
      `push.py:418` and init.py's `_git` are reused. Verified by inspection and by the config
      schema being unchanged in this story.

file_impact.reason: Add _require_s3_helper_if_s3_url(remote_url) (pure scheme check -> require_s3_helper) and call it in push_tickets_branch: in the synchronous always path after the existing remote-url resolution at line ~418, and in the async arm before detaching. Fails closed unconditionally on s3://|s3+zip:// remotes.
Add require_s3_helper_if_s3_remote(repo, remote, run_git_fn) that resolves the remote URL via the existing run_git and calls push._require_s3_helper_if_s3_url; keeps init.py within the 800-LOC cap.

Add exactly one call line at the top of _mount_or_create_branch (after remote_name is resolved) to _init_probe.require_s3_helper_if_s3_remote, so an s3:// misconfiguration fails closed at setup. init.py is at the 800-LOC cap: exactly one line added.

New integration tests: missing/too-old helper on s3:// and s3+zip:// remotes fails closed with the actionable message on push and init; non-s3 and unresolvable remotes are no-ops; async arm fails in the parent before detaching.

compiled_state.title: Fail closed when an s3:// ticket remote is used without a locking git-remote-s3 helper
